parameters.query:
select id as business_id, business_name, gbp_account_id, location_id
from businesses
where status = 'Active'
  and gbp_account_id is not null
  and location_id is not null;

nodes.name: List Reviews for Location
nodes.notes: onError: continueErrorOutput so a bad gbp_account_id/location_id for one business (Google 400/403/404) routes to this node's error output instead of aborting the whole scheduled run for every other business. The error output's item is just {error: "..."} -- business_id etc. are NOT preserved on it, and pairedItem/itemMatching lookups back to 'Get Active Businesses with GBP' are documented as unreliable specifically across HTTP Request's error output (n8n issues #30050, #12558). Fixed by re-pairing via 'Pair Failure with Business (by position)' below instead of any reach-back expression.

nodes.name: Pair Failure with Business (by position)
nodes.notes: Input 0: the failed item(s) from List Reviews for Location's error output. Input 1: the original business rows from Get Active Businesses with GBP, in the same order. Both lists share the same 1:1 order/length (one HTTP call per business row), so 'Combine By Position' reliably re-attaches business_id/business_name to a failure without relying on pairedItem, which n8n does not preserve across this node's error output.

parameters.query: update businesses set last_sync_error = $1, last_sync_error_at = now() where id = $2;

nodes.name: Log GBP Fetch Failure
nodes.notes: Records a broken GBP link (bad account/location id, revoked OAuth, etc.) on the business row so it's queryable instead of only visible in n8n's execution log. business_id comes from the position-paired merge upstream, not a reach-back expression. Does not notify the business directly.

parameters.query: select id as existing_activity_id, activity_status as existing_status from activities where review_id = '{{ $json.review_id }}' limit 1;

with candidate as (
  select c.id as customer_id, c.full_name,
         similarity(lower(c.full_name), lower($1)) as name_score
  from customers c
  join activities a on a.customer_id = c.id and a.activity_type = 'Request Sent'
  where c.business_id = $2
    and a.timestamp >= now() - interval '60 days'
  order by name_score desc, a.timestamp desc
  limit 1
),
fallback as (
  select id as customer_id, full_name, 0::float as name_score
  from customers
  where business_id = $2
    and source = 'system'
    and full_name = 'Unmatched Reviewer'
  limit 1
)
select customer_id, full_name, name_score from candidate where name_score >= 0.3
union all
select customer_id, full_name, name_score from fallback
where not exists (select 1 from candidate where name_score >= 0.3)
limit 1;

nodes.name: Find Best Match Customer
nodes.notes: Requires the pg_trgm extension for similarity(). Matches must score >= 0.3 to count as real; otherwise falls back to that business's 'Unmatched Reviewer' placeholder customer. Requires the placeholder row to already exist per business (see 'Ensure Placeholder Customer' step in onboarding, or run once per business manually).

"Auto-matched to " + $json.matched_full_name + " (name_score: " + $json.name_score + ")" : "No confident match (reviewer: " + $json.reviewer_name + ") \u2014 logged against Unmatched Reviewer placeholder") + " via GBP review capture workflow"] }}

nodes.name: Already Replied on Google?
nodes.notes: Checks reviewReply on the raw GBP API response (attached in Flatten Reviews as has_existing_google_reply). Prevents re-generating/re-posting a reply for a review that already has one on Google -- e.g. replied manually, by a previous system, or before this automation existed on a business with existing review history. True -> just mark Completed and notify (no AI reply, no post). False -> proceeds to the normal Good Review?/AI-reply flow as before.

parameters.query: update activities set reply_text = $1, activity_status = 'Completed', notes = notes || ' | Skipped auto-reply: review already had a reply on Google' where id = $2;

nodes.name: Log Already-Replied (Skip AI Reply)
nodes.notes: Records the reply that already existed on Google (not one this workflow generated) and marks the activity Completed immediately, since no further action is needed -- no AI call, no Post Reply to GBP.

nodes.name: Generate AI Reply
nodes.notes: Model corrected from gemini-2.5-flash (deprecated, returns 'no longer available to new users' 404 as of testing on 2026-08-20) to gemini-3.6-flash. If this model is deprecated in turn, check https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models for the current text-generation model name -- do not silently retry the old name.

nodes.name: Extract Reply Text
nodes.notes: Falls back to a fixed template if Gemini fails or returns an unexpected shape, so a bad AI call never blocks the reply from being posted.

parameters.query: =update activities set reply_text = '{{ $('Extract Reply Text').item.json.reply_text.replace(/'/g, "''") }}', activity_status = 'Completed' where id = '{{ $('Attach Activity ID').item.json.activity_id }}';
=update activities set notes = notes || ' | LOW STAR - needs manual reply' where id = '{{ $json.activity_id }}';
